validated_results.title: Enhanced inhibition of prostate cancer xenograft tumor growth by combining quercetin and green tea.
validated_results.reason: This is a preclinical xenograft experiment in SCID mice with LAPC-4 cells, not a human study of tea intake and incident prostate cancer.

validated_results.title: Chemopreventive effect of quercetin in MNU and testosterone induced prostate cancer of Sprague-Dawley rats.
validated_results.reason: Quercetin was administered to MNU/testosterone-treated Sprague-Dawley rats, so the evidence is exclusively animal.

validated_results.title: Dietary patterns and prostate cancer risk: report from the population based ULSAM cohort study of Swedish men.
validated_results.reason: Prospective ULSAM cohort of Swedish men reporting prostate cancer incidence in relation to adherence to a modified Mediterranean Diet Score assessed by 7-day food records.

extraction.comparison_type: high or medium versus low adherence to the modified Mediterranean Diet Score
extraction.population: Adult men in the Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men (ULSAM) cohort

sample_size.excerpt: Food intake data in the Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men cohort was determined by 7-day food records. Adherence to a modified Mediterranean Diet Score (mMDS) and a low carbohydrate-high protein (LCHP) score were grouped as low, medium, or high in the whole study population (n = 1,044) and in those identified as adequate reporters of energy intake (n = 566), respectively.

cases.excerpt: There were no associations between dietary patterns and prostate cancer (n = 133) in the whole study population.

comparison.excerpt: Adherence to a modified Mediterranean Diet Score (mMDS) and a low carbohydrate-high protein (LCHP) score were grouped as low, medium, or high

design.excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was analyzed with Cox proportional hazard regression (median follow-up 13 years)

continent.excerpt: report from the population based ULSAM cohort study of Swedish men

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Food intake data in the Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men cohort was determined by 7-day food records.

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: ci_lower, ci_upper, effect_size, effect_type, p_value

validated_results.title: Effects of α-tocopherol and β-carotene supplementation on cancer incidence and mortality: 18-year postintervention follow-up of the Alpha-tocopherol, Beta-carotene Cancer Prevention Study.
validated_results.reason: Postintervention follow-up of the randomized ATBC trial reporting cancer incidence, including prostate cancer, among beta-carotene recipients versus nonrecipients.

extraction.comparison_type: beta-carotene (20 mg daily) recipients compared with nonrecipients

sample_size.excerpt: To determine the postintervention effects of α-tocopherol and β-carotene, 25,563 men were followed 18 years for cancer incidence and all causes of mortality through national registers.

cases.excerpt: For prostate cancer (n = 2,321), RR was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.89-1.05) among α-tocopherol recipients compared with nonrecipients with the preventive effect of α-tocopherol continuing ∼8 years postintervention.

comparison.excerpt: β-carotene (20 mg) increased risk of lung cancer and overall mortality

design.excerpt: 18-year postintervention follow-up of the Alpha-tocopherol, Beta-carotene Cancer Prevention Study

timing.excerpt: 25,563 men were followed 18 years for cancer incidence and all causes of mortality through national registers

continent.excerpt: In the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study among 29,133 Finnish male smokers

exposure_measurement.excerpt: daily α-tocopherol (50 mg) for a median of 6.1 years decreased the risk of prostate cancer, whereas β-carotene (20 mg) increased risk of lung cancer

validated_results.title: Effects of α-tocopherol and β-carotene supplementation on cancer incidence and mortality: 18-year postintervention follow-up of the Alpha-tocopherol, Beta-carotene Cancer Prevention Study.
validated_results.reason: Postintervention follow-up of the randomized ATBC trial reporting a prostate cancer incidence relative risk for alpha-tocopherol recipients versus nonrecipients.

extraction.comparison_type: alpha-tocopherol (50 mg daily) recipients compared with nonrecipients

sample_size.excerpt: To determine the postintervention effects of α-tocopherol and β-carotene, 25,563 men were followed 18 years for cancer incidence and all causes of mortality through national registers.

cases.excerpt: For prostate cancer (n = 2,321), RR was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.89-1.05) among α-tocopherol recipients compared with nonrecipients with the preventive effect of α-tocopherol continuing ∼8 years postintervention.
